label: Late-episode ramp unit; deviations scale with ramp: a1 choice, a2/S1 at D2, last outcome
terms: np.exp((ep_trial-99)/20) * (phase == GO) * np.tanh(choice) ;; np.exp((ep_trial-99)/20) * (phase == D2) * table(3*action+state, {4: 0, 5: -1, 7: 1, 8: 0.5}) ;; np.exp((ep_trial-99)/20) * (phase == D1) * table(4*prev_action+2*prev_state+prev_reward, {7: 16, 6: -22, 9: 37, 8: -18, 13: 4, 12: -37, 11: 40, 10: -12}) ;; np.exp((ep_trial-99)/20) * (phase == GO) * table(4*prev_action+2*prev_state+prev_reward, {7: 72, 6: -15, 9: 5, 8: -21, 13: -28, 12: -52, 11: 18, 10: -45}) ;; np.exp((ep_trial-99)/20) * (phase == D2) * table(4*prev_action+2*prev_state+prev_reward, {7: -10, 6: 10, 9: -6, 8: 31, 13: -12, 12: 22, 11: -8, 10: 20})
explanation: GRU candidate unit 18 is dominated by a steep late-episode ramp (timing R^2 0.90; the D1 mean goes from -0.95 to -0.17). The residual effects all grow with that ramp, so every term is multiplied by exp((ep_trial-99)/20). Unscaled versions of the same terms reach only 0.10 R^2 beyond timing on dev. At GO the unit is higher when the policy favours a1 (tanh of the policy logit; the actual upcoming action fits the same). At D2 it is higher after a2 (a2->S1 rare highest, a2->S2 common positive) and lower after a1->S2 rare. Signed tables over the last trial (choice, state, reward), one per phase, carry the rest. At D1 it is raised after rewarded trials and after rare-rewarded ones most (a2 S1 r, a1 S2 r) and lowered after unrewarded ones (a2 S2 u, a1 S1 u). At GO it is high after a1 S1 r and low after a2 S2 u / a2 S1 u. At D2 it is slightly higher after unrewarded trials. Hidden good state, trials since reversal and future reward add little. The model value term adds only about 0.01. Test R^2 beyond timing 0.40 (dev 0.38), above the additive 'all' ceiling of 0.29 because of the ramp scaling. No future variables are used: at GO the policy logit stands in for the upcoming action. Remaining misses: windows near the episode end with long reward streaks, where the unit is higher than predicted.
